arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: The landowner's counsel stated the case concerns the extent of Nollan and Dolan review for excessive exactions.
The district's counsel emphasized that applying these standards would radically change standard regulatory programs.
The Solicitor General's counsel noted the parties agree Florida may require mitigation for wetland destruction.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on whether the Nollan and Dolan legal standards apply to monetary conditions. The landowner wants to test the fee's proportionality. The district wants to preserve its regulatory authority.

The district wants the Court to reject the lawsuit and uphold the fee as a valid regulatory condition.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The landowner argues that Nollan and Dolan review applies to monetary conditions imposed during discretionary land-use approvals.
The district argues that applying Nollan and Dolan to general regulatory programs would radically change how agencies operate.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Ginsburg asked if a landowner has a claim when an agency denies a permit without requiring mitigation.
Justice Sotomayor questioned why the case is before the Court if the conservation offer was not considered mitigation.

paragraphs: This case defines the scope of constitutional challenges to permit conditions. It determines whether landowners can sue over monetary demands. It affects how agencies structure land-use regulations.
